source.check: returned unopposed: 'all the members were returned unopposed for the County Council' and all but two re-nominated (Impartial Reporter, 22 May 1958, p. 7); named on the Finance Committee at the annual meeting of 11 July 1958 (Fermanagh Herald, 12 July 1958, p. 5)

note: Triennial election of Fermanagh County Council, polled Thursday 5 June 1958. No contests: the Impartial Reporter of 22 May 1958, p. 7, states that 'all the members were returned unopposed for the County Council and the three Rural Councils', and that the new council shows two changes only — Mr. Thomas J. Morrow succeeds Mr. Thomas Creddan in Lisbellaw, and Mr. Mark Breen succeeds Mr. Denis Leonard in Derrylea — 'all the other members have been re-nominated'. The unchanged members are recorded where a selection list or a report of the new council's meetings names them, each division inferred from the 1955 return. The 1955 source is the Fermanagh Herald's full nomination list, 4 June 1955, p. 8. Division names follow the 1955 return. Crum is recorded for Mr. Cahir Healy, M.P., not for the 1955 member. The Belfast News-Letter of 20 February 1958, p. 4, reports that Healy 'has been elected a member of Fermanagh County Council to fill the vacancy caused by the death of Mr. James Goodwin, who represented the county electoral division of Crum'. Healy was therefore the sitting member for Crum at the June election, and the paper's statement that all members other than the two named were re-nominated covers him. Filled from the Impartial Reporter's reports of Unionist selections (1, 8 and 15 May 1958): Lisnaskea; each was returned unopposed (Impartial Reporter, 22 May 1958, p. 7). Recorded for Nationalist-held divisions from the selection lists and first-meeting reports in the Fermanagh Herald: Doon, Innismacsaint and Irvinestown. Recorded from reports of the new council's meetings during the term: Ballinamallard, Lack, Maguiresbridge, Florencecourt, Enniskillen Borough, Enniskillen Rural, Brookeborough, Holywell and Roslea. Division inferred from the by-election of February 1958, when he was elected for Crum on the death of Mr. James Goodwin (Belfast News-Letter, 20 February 1958, p. 4); the Fermanagh Herald, 12 July 1958, p. 5 names him ('Healy') on the Finance Committee at the new council's annual meeting. Returned unopposed.
